subject: Why is anova() not using the "robust" chi-square?

messages.author: ec12e510d7b112ad
messages.subject: Why is anova() not using the "robust" chi-square?
parts:
I´m comparing two different nested models estimated with the WLSMV estimator. If I use anova(model1, model2) to compare these models, the function returns the results based on the non-robust column in the summary output. 
Why does that happen? that does´t make any sense to me.

Thank you. 
Tobias

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Why is anova() not using the "robust" chi-square?
parts:
You do not give us any output, so I will have to guess that you mean
that anova() is using the difference between the non-corrected (naive)
chi-square test statistics.

That is as intended. It is this difference (between the naive test
statistics) that we scale, to get a scaled difference test.

See the references in ?lavTestLRT

Yves.
